messages:
sophia: Heads-up — found a weird conversion failure when bringing up a HF chat_template into Redwood prompt format. System role text is getting duplicated on every assistant reply in our Redwood tests.
lee: Can you paste the original jinja template you used?

sophia: Sure, simplified repro:
```jinja
{% set persona = "helpful assistant" %}
{"role":"system","content":"You are a {{ persona }}."}
{"role":"user","content":"{{ user_prompt }}"}
```

sophia: After our conversion pipeline we emit something like:
```text
<|system|>You are a helpful assistant.<|endoftext|>
<|user|>{{ user_prompt }}
```
When sending that to the Redwood runtime, {{ user_prompt }} ends up empty at conversion time (we call the Jinja renderer with an empty context) and the system sentence gets duplicated in the assistant output: "You are a helpful assistant.You are a helpful assistant." :confused:
rahul: Sounds like two potential problems: (A) our converter is rendering Jinja templates instead of leaving placeholders; (B) role markers / special tokens are interacting badly with tokenizers or KV cache. Do we call jinja.render anywhere? :thinking_face:
maria: I traced the flow quickly. Our converter calls parse_chat_template() -> jinja_render(context=None) -> role_map() -> add_role_markers(). So yes, jinja_render(None) is executed (bug). Also I compared tokenization between HF tokenizer and the Redwood runtime tokenizer: the same system sentence produces different token ids because the HF model's config.json defined a BOS/EOS token that we inadvertently keep when we add role markers. Repro I ran locally:
```
hf_ids = hf_tok.encode("You are a helpful assistant.")
red_ids = rw_tok.encode("You are a helpful assistant.")
# hf_ids starts with 50256 (special) vs red_ids does not
```
That shifts KV cache alignment and can produce repeated prefixes when generating.
lee: Ok so root causes: 1) Jinja placeholders being rendered/cleared during conversion; 2) role markers / special token differences between HF config.json and Redwood tokenization. Both plausible to cause duplication. Which code path strips braces?

sophia: It's the unconditional jinja_render step. I can patch to only render when a non-empty context is provided or when user opts into template rendering. Quick patch: skip jinja_render if context is None and mark template as raw. Also add a regression test that ensures {{ user_prompt }} remains verbatim in the converted prompt.
rahul: For the tokenizer side, we should consult model config.json for keys: "bos_token", "eos_token", "add_special_tokens" and make role marker injection model-aware. Short term workaround: strip known special token ids from the sequence when composing prefix for the runtime (e.g., drop leading 50256 if model defines it). Long term: prefer structured metadata for roles instead of inserting printable markers.
maria: As a manual workaround you can wrap the chat_template in raw tags so Jinja won't touch it when pipeline runs, e.g.:
```jinja
{% raw %}{"role":"system","content":"You are a {{ persona }}."}{% endraw %}
```
But that's annoying for template authors. Better to fix converter.
sophia: I opened a PR branch (fix/jinja-skip-render) with the skip logic + unit tests: 1) canonical template conversion keeps {{ user_prompt }} verbatim; 2) tokenization parity test between HF and Redwood tokenizers for system role samples. Dev pipeline ran: dev-bot: deploy-preview succeeded on branch fix/jinja-skip-render.
lee: Nice. Action items: sophia to finish PR + add a test that compares generation outputs before/after conversion for a small toy model; rahul to add a small shim that removes model-specific special tokens when computing prefix token ids; docs: add a note to the onboarding checklist about role markers and tokenizers. I'll add those to the model-onboarding board.
sophia: Thanks — I'll ping eng-runtime and eng-ml for review. Anyone seen any weirdness when testing quantized variants? Does quantization change tokenization?
rahul: Quantization doesn't change the tokenizer itself, but it can change numeric stability which sometimes amplifies prefix-injection issues. So fixing the template/token mapping should resolve the symptom across quantized variants.
maria: Triaged and added to the board. Closing out for now once PR merges.
